expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: export type Subscription = | (SubscriptionBase & { status: "trialing"; trialEndsAt: Date; }) | ... — discriminated on status

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Each status branch has only its relevant fields; canceled only has cancelReason and voluntary

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: assertNever function with default: return assertNever(sub) in the switch

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: type SubscriptionId = Brand<string, "SubscriptionId">; type CustomerId = Brand<string, "CustomerId">;

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: States 'this type says nothing about which transitions are legal' and provides only a TODO placeholder with no implementation

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Insight section explicitly names: retryCount inaccessible until narrowed to past_due, assertNever catches new statuses, ID swaps become compile errors

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Misuse enumeration first item rejects the flat optional-fields approach
